messages:
claire: Heads-up — we're seeing span gaps for jobs that cross the gateway -> upload-worker async hop. traces for user uploads end at gateway, workers start new traces. Noticed after the OTLP collector change last week.
kevin: hmm. did the gateway stop setting trace headers on the SQS message attrs? any examples of the message payload we saw?
claire: example from CloudWatch logs:
```
MessageAttributes: {
  traceparent: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: '00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' },
  baggage: { DataType: 'String', StringValue: 'user_id=12345;env=prod' }
}
```
but upload-worker's collector shows spans with new trace ids.
maria: do uploads call our gateway->ingest directly or route via api-gw v2? we changed header normalization in v2.
ashok: api-gw v2 strips unknown headers by default unless configured. traceparent is RFC-defined but baggage was being copied into a custom header 'x-rw-baggage' — that might have been dropped.
claire: confirmed: gateway was using x-rw-baggage and we removed forwarding in the gateway config. traceparent still present in attrs for most messages but some retries show only partial attrs.
samir: retries may come from the Lambda retry wrapper which republishs with only body and MessageAttributes gets lost. That's a behavior of the retry helper.
tia: so two problems: (1) header attr loss on retry/republish, (2) baggage forwarding isn't reliable and is often large — we should avoid sending entire baggage across SQS.
kevin: proposal: always set traceparent in MessageAttributes (small, fixed size) and replace baggage with a small 'baggage-hash' key. Collector/ingest can fetch full baggage from a short-term store if needed.
maria: I like baggage-hash idea. but storing/extracting baggage requires a low-LAT store and writes on the hot path — could add latency. alternative: only forward essential tags (user_id, request_origin) as dedicated attrs and drop free-form baggage.
ashok: we should also ensure OTLP spans include a 'link' to original trace instead of trying to continue the same parent when we can't guarantee header fidelity. That avoids creating orphan spans while preserving relationship.
claire: example worker behavior suggested:
```
if (msg.attrs.traceparent) {
  ctx = parseTraceparent(msg.attrs.traceparent)
  startSpan('worker.process', { links: [{ traceId: ctx.traceId }] })
} else {
  startSpan('worker.process')
}
```
then export with a link to original trace id.
samir: exporter debate: send OTLP/gRPC directly from workers to vendor or hop through our internal collector? if retention cost is a concern we want central sampling decisions.
tia: central collector wins for retention and batch sampling. workers should OTLP->internal-collector; collector applies tail-sampling and drops low-value traces before long-term storage.
kevin: downside: extra hop increases latency for live debug. but most async jobs don't need sub-second trace availability. we can keep a small hot-path stream for critical spans.
maria: another gotcha: SQS message attribute size limit. We must not exceed 256KB in attributes. baggage frequently breaches that if we try to shove everything.
ashok: action items:
- Gateway: ensure traceparent attribute always set before enqueue (kevin) — due EOD 1718080000
- Gateway: stop forwarding arbitrary x-rw-baggage; instead write critical tags to dedicated attrs (claire + maria) — due 1718160000
- Workers: when missing parent, create link-span instead of forcing new root (ashok) — due 1718120000
- Collector: implement baggage-hash fetch endpoint + short TTL store prototype (samir) — due 1718240000
- Document best-practice for retry wrappers to preserve MessageAttributes (tia) — due 1718190000
ingest-bot: deploy-notes: collector tail-sampling config PR exists at https://git.redwood/infra/collector/pulls/42 — review requested.
claire: thanks — will follow up with minimal schema for 'essential attrs' (user_id, org_id, env, trace_flags) and a short example for SDKs.
kevin: one more note: metrics pipeline unaffected. traces are the concern here. :thumbsup:
maria: +1. we'll iterate on baggage-minimization and keep links until we have robust attr preservation.
ashok: cool. I'll draft a small design doc for 'link-first' async tracing approach and post in #eng-platform tomorrow.
claire: great, closing loop here. if anyone sees new orphan traces after the gateway patch ping me.
